text:
ana: Anyone seeing packet loss between GPU pods in us-west-2? Started right after the 03:05 config deploy — intra-node pings to inference pods dropping ~40%
oncall-bot: alert: net-latency-high on cluster-gpu-3 — packet loss avg 35% — paging #eng-infra
pradeep: checking. are the affected pods in the same AZ/nodes? any netpol changes pushed recently?
ana: nodes are same AZ. we applied a Calico policy via Terraform at ~03:00 to tighten egress for ml-team namespace. snippet from the tf change: 
```yaml
resource "kubernetes_network_policy" "ml_team_restrict" {
  metadata {
    name = "ml-team-restrict"
    namespace = "ml-team"
  }
  spec {
    pod_selector = {} # oops this is empty in the TF plan
    policy_types = ["Egress"]
    egress = []
  }
}
```
sasha: can you paste `kubectl get networkpolicy ml-team-restrict -n ml-team -o yaml` or calicoctl output? Calico can end up shadowing traffic if selectors are too broad.
nana: pasted output from the cluster: 
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: ml-team-restrict
  namespace: ml-team
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress: []
```
pradeep: yep — `podSelector: {}` + `policyTypes: [Egress]` with an empty egress list == deny all egress for every pod in ml-team. we intended to target pods with `role: inference`. label mismatch in the tf var caused this.
kai: that would explain east-west issues. RDMA-over-IP and our inter-pod TCP/UDP for KV sync get dropped if egress is denied.
nana: rolling back the tf change now — patching to set `pod_selector.matchLabels: {role: inference}` and allow egress to namespaceSelector for gpu-fab. applying: 
```bash
# quick patch to undo broad deny
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: ml-team-restrict
  namespace: ml-team
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      role: inference
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          team: gpu-fab
EOF
```
deploy-bot: terraform apply completed at 03:24 — ml-team-restrict updated
sasha: monitoring, can you run `ping`/`iperf` between two of the previously failing pods?
nana: pre-rollback ping from inference-0 -> inference-3: 
```
PING 10.42.3.12 (10.42.3.12): 56 data bytes
--- 10.42.3.12 ping statistics ---
10 packets transmitted, 6 received, 40% packet loss, time 9000ms
```
nana: post-rollback ping: 
```
PING 10.42.3.12 (10.42.3.12): 56 data bytes
--- 10.42.3.12 ping statistics ---
10 packets transmitted, 10 received, 0% packet loss, time 9000ms
```
pradeep: good — rollback confirmed. I'll file a short postmortem: root cause = TF networkpolicy defaulting to empty podSelector; mitigations: policy linter in CI, require non-empty podSelector for egress policies, add canary deploys for netpol changes.
kai: :thumbsup: also add a Calico dry-run + stage gate for policy changes, plus an automated test that pings a cross-node pod in staging for every netpol change.
nana: will follow up with the PR to add the linter rule and the staging check. thanks all.
